assumptions: RDKit's FindMCS defaults unless the two ring options are set.
limits: One core for the whole set: a library of two unrelated series has a small MCS, which is the finding, not a failure.
A timeout returns the best core found so far, flagged as a lower bound rather than the maximum.
bio.jane/contract.question: What is the largest substructure all of these molecules share?

description: The maximum common substructure of a set of small molecules (RDKit FindMCS): the largest core every structure shares, as SMARTS, with its atom and bond count.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

complete_rings_only.description: a ring is in the core whole or not at all — the core a chemist would draw. Off, RDKit may return a partial ring, which is a valid substructure and a strange thing to call a scaffold.

molecules.description: the structures: one SMILES or molfile per entry.

ring_matches_ring_only.description: a ring atom only matches another ring atom, so a chain carbon never maps onto a ring one.

timeout.description: seconds before RDKit stops searching. The MCS problem is NP-hard, so a large diverse set can run long; a run that stops early reports its core as a lower bound. In s. Advanced.

name: find_common_substructure

canceled.description: the search hit the timeout, so this core is a LOWER BOUND and a longer run may find a larger one

smarts.description: the common core as SMARTS — wire it into decompose_r_groups as `core`

summary.description: the common core in words, generated from this run

unread.description: input indices RDKit could not read
